Hi Alice — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Ben (legal/privsec) and Marissa (forensics/ops) to confirm specifics. High-level answers below; we will follow up with a short packet and an evidence map by EOD Monday.

1) Notification timing: Our standard DPA language uses a 72-hour initial notification target for incidents that materially affect customer data confidentiality or integrity. That window is subject to reasonable operational constraints (for example, ongoing live containment activities or law enforcement interactions). In practice we aim to provide an initial status within 72 hours for EU customers and a fuller technical summary within 10 business days.

2) Evidence/export ownership: Redwood takes operational responsibility for producing platform-side artifacts (audit logs, telemetry slices, storage metadata). For captures that require customer data extraction from a subprocessor (e.g., third-party storage or analytics vendors), Redwood will coordinate the request and provide the transport package, but final handover may require the subprocessor's exports and their permissions. We typically document the handoff owner in the forensic request (see attached template).

Planned deliverables: evidence mapping XLSX, redwood process doc (subprocessor escalation steps), and a short cover note for procurement that explains what we can guarantee contractually vs operationally.

Ben / Marissa — can you confirm the language we should share for: a) absolute notification exceptions (law enforcement, national security orders) and b) a short paragraph on escrow/forensic-snapshot availability (time-to-export estimates)?

Olga
Olga Petrov

Thanks, Olga. Draft guidance below — copying the paragraph into the packet we will send to FinServCorp.

-----
Notification exceptions and limits (draft contract-friendly language):
Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customers with an initial notification of a Security Incident that materially affects Customer Data within 72 hours of discovery. In certain circumstances — including when active containment or law enforcement engagement is required — Redwood may delay initial disclosures for a short, reasonable period to avoid interfering with remediation or legal processes. Redwood will notify the Customer of any delay and the expected timing for an update.

Forensic evidence and subprocessor exports:
Redwood will provide platform-produced artifacts (system audit logs, telemetry captures, runtime snapshots) and will cooperate with Customers and their designated forensic partners to the extent permitted under applicable law and third-party agreements. Where evidence resides with a subcontractor, Redwood will initiate and manage the export request and provide the Customer with the export package as soon as practicable; however, the timeline may be impacted by the subprocessor's own procedures and legal obligations. Redwood can offer escrowed-forensic-snapshot services (see schedule A) as a contractual add-on to guarantee quicker handover timeframes.
-----

Marissa — can you please attach the forensic-snapshot guidance and realistic timelines (we typically estimate 24-72 hours for platform artifacts, 5-14 days for subprocessor exports depending on jurisdiction). I'll add a short note on liability: we accept operational responsibility for coordinating evidence production but cannot compel a third-party subprocessor's internal approvals unless expressly specified in the subprocessor agreement.

Ben

Hi Alice — attaching the evidence mapping and a short forensic-snapshot guidance doc (see Drive link below). Short summary here:

- Platform artifacts (audit logs, KV-access traces, runtime counters): typically available and exportable within 24-72 hours after an incident triage is complete.
